correctness.rationale: The linear mean/difference coordinate change exactly splits the weighted loss, reducing two-row anti-Monge projection to weighted isotonic regression on the differences. On each pooled block the top and bottom Jacobian absolute row sums are 1+2[b_j/(a_j+b_j)](1-c_j/C_B) and 1+2[a_j/(a_j+b_j)](1-c_j/C_B); C_B≤C gives the claimed global upper bound. Strictly descending data differences lie inside a full-pooling open KKT cell, and an exact sign perturbation attains the bound. An elementary minimum-c and α≥1/2 argument with equality rigidity yields 2−1/m uniquely at equal weights; strict α<1 and c_j/C>0 give <3; a continuous weight path reaches every intermediate value and approaches 3. The extracted exact-fraction checker ran and reported 12883 assertions passed. Universal results rest on proof, not finite tests.

value.rationale: Two-row Monge/anti-Monge regression is a natural minimal nontrivial multivariate shape-constrained estimator. Its sharp max-coordinate input-to-output error amplification matters for bounded independent observation perturbations, which mean-square statistical risk and Hilbert-norm contractivity do not control sharply. The exact heteroscedastic formula exhibits a natural and sharp robustness design principle (equal weights uniquely minimize) and a nontrivial unbounded-weight degradation approaching three; this quantitative boundary case can guide stability analysis for larger Monge cones.
